content.text: Complete assignment thoroughly: implementation-audit of feat/add-reset (verbatim F2 brief).

## 1. Goal and behavioural contract
Satisfied. `src/counter.js:11-14` returns the previous count and deletes only the selected key. Existing zero-default reads make deletion observably equivalent to resetting to zero. `README.md:5` accurately documents usage.

## 2. Correctness, regressions, architecture, wire contracts
Reviewed the complete supplied diff, implementation, tests, package configuration, and plan. Reset preserves the existing Map key semantics and allows subsequent increments to restart at 1. No cross-file inconsistencies, unnecessary abstractions, or substantiated correctness defects found.

## 3. Security and privacy delta
None. The change adds an in-memory operation without credentials, authorization, external I/O, or personal-data handling.

## 4. Verification adequacy
Read all six QA captures, including passing suite output and both failing mutants. Tests exercise the actual exported implementation, previous-count returns, name isolation, and unknown names. QA4–QA6 additionally demonstrate period restart and edge cases. No checks were rerun.

Note: `test/counter.test.js:12-26` lacks permanent assertions for increment-after-reset and repeated reset. Non-blocking because those behaviors are demonstrated in QA4–QA6 and supported by the implementation; retaining automated guards would strengthen regression coverage.

## 5. Final assessment
No blockers found. Assessment covers implementation correctness and supplied verification, not validation of the subsequently assembled merge-gate record.

REVIEW-TRAILER-v1
invocation: implementation-audit
sections_covered: 1,2,3,4,5
model_id: onara/cx/gpt-6.1-sol
security_delta: no
verdict: PASS
blockers: none
adversarial_criteria:
- invariant: Incrementing a previously reset name starts its next period at 1 rather than continuing its old sequence.
  positive_witness: After three login increments and reset, increment(login) returns 1 and get(login) returns 1, as captured in QA4.
  negative_control: Retaining stale increment state makes the next increment return 4; this MUST fail the criterion.
  observable: QA4 and QA6 capture post-reset increment results of 1; the negative control is hypothetical, not executed by this reviewer.
  boundary: Exported Counter API through consecutive reset, increment, and get calls.
END-REVIEW-TRAILER
